solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Something spicy for starters, made by expert (4)

indicatorNotes.for starters: take only the starting letter of 'made'

annotation.surface: A chef lets an expert make the spicy starters.
annotation.walkthrough: 'For starters' looks like the menu's first course; it only takes the first letter of the next word.
annotation.definitionFit: Mace is a spice made from the lacy covering of the nutmeg seed.

entries.clue: Married twice, gauges somehow it’s a futile endeavour (4,4)

indicatorNotes.somehow: the letters come together in some unstated way

blocks.note: M = married, as in genealogies, taken twice

annotation.surface: Someone who has married twice decides that measuring anything is pointless.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Married twice' sounds like a weary divorcee's history, but it is just two Ms to add to the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A mug's game is an activity only a fool (a mug) would take on, since it cannot pay off.

entries.clue: Church is welcoming poor country’s folk (8)

indicatorNotes.is welcoming: IS takes LEAN in, as a host welcomes a guest

blocks.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for church
taken as written, opened up to hold LEAN
lean as in a poor, meagre year

annotation.surface: A church opens its doors to people from an impoverished nation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Poor country' reads as one phrase; split it, since 'poor' is LEAN and 'country's folk' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the folk of Chile, the poor country of the surface, are its nationals.

entries.clue: Grass up old lag, getting time inside as such? (10)

annotation.definition: Grass up old lag, getting time inside as such?

indicatorNotes.inside: 'inside' is slang for in prison, and here it literally puts T inside LIFER

blocks.note: to shop someone is to inform on them to the police
an old lag is a long-serving convict, a lifer

annotation.surface: An informer betrays a veteran prisoner, who ends up doing time for a petty crime.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a lifer grassed up and jailed for it could well be a shoplifter. 'Grass' is British slang for informer, and 'old lag' for a habitual convict.
annotation.definitionFit: A shoplifter is exactly the sort of offender who might be grassed up and given time inside.

entries.clue: It may be concealed by varnishing edge (5)

annotation.definition: It may be concealed by varnishing edge

indicatorNotes.concealed by: the answer lies hidden in the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words: the tail of the first and the head of the second

annotation.surface: A cabinet-maker notes that a fitting can be disguised when the edge is varnished.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: a hinge really can be concealed along a cupboard edge, and the letters are concealed in 'varnishing edge'.
annotation.definitionFit: A concealed hinge sits out of sight at the edge of a door.

entries.clue: Form of verb is beyond many English (4,5)

blocks.note: beyond = past, as in 'past the church'

annotation.surface: A grammar note on a verb form lying outside many English rules.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Is' sits as a link between definition and wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: The past tense is the form of a verb for what has already happened.

entries.clue: Mark seen in the middle of hammock? (8,5)

annotation.definition: Mark seen in the middle of hammock?

blocks.note: reads as a stain on the fabric; it is a punctuation mark

blocks.clueFragment: seen in the middle of hammock?
blocks.note: look at the letters, not the object: the centre of the word, read upwards in a down entry, spells a familiar punctuation mark

annotation.surface: Someone spots a mark in the centre of a hammock.
annotation.walkthrough: The middle of 'hammock' spells AMMOC, which is COMMA upside down, so what you see there is literally an inverted comma. The question mark flags the joke.
annotation.definitionFit: A mark in writing is a punctuation sign, and the quotation mark gets this name from looking like a comma turned upside down.

entries.clue: Blimey — hemmed in by river in both directions! (3-3)

indicatorNotes.hemmed in by: WOW sits inside TAY, fenced in on both sides

annotation.surface: An astonished boater finds the river blocked at both ends.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blimey' is British slang for surprise; WOW does the same job.
annotation.definitionFit: Two-way means going or working in both directions, like two-way traffic.

entries.clue: Equality with king usurping power is an uncommon thing (6)

indicatorNotes.usurping: to usurp is to seize someone's place, so R takes P's spot

annotation.surface: A king seizing power on equal terms with his people would be unusual indeed.
annotation.walkthrough: The political surface of kings and usurped power hides a one-letter swap.
annotation.definitionFit: A rarity is something seldom found.

entries.clue: One’s legendary in performing musical phrases back to front (7)

indicatorNotes.back to front: the letter at the back moves to the front

blocks.note: riffing is playing riffs, short repeated musical phrases

annotation.surface: A musician becomes a legend by playing phrases backwards.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Back to front' does not reverse the word: only the final G moves to the front of RIFFING.
annotation.definitionFit: The griffin is a legendary beast, part eagle and part lion.

entries.clue: One vessel capsized in curious Scottish loch — foul play? (5,8)

indicatorNotes.capsized: a capsized boat is upside down, so I SUB reads up the column
indicatorNotes.in: BUSI goes between FUNNY and NESS

annotation.surface: A boat overturns on a strange Scottish loch, and someone suspects sabotage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Curious Scottish loch' makes you think of the monster; 'curious' and 'loch' are separate pieces with the capsized sub between them. Loch Ness is the famous lake in the Scottish Highlands.
annotation.definitionFit: Funny business is underhand or dishonest dealing; the question mark admits foul play is one kind.

entries.clue: Defender turned to protect area, leading 5-1 (7)

indicatorNotes.to protect: SOUR wraps round the rest, shielding it
indicatorNotes.leading: what leads goes first, so A stands at the head of VI

blocks.note: milk that has turned has gone sour
5 and 1 in Roman numerals, V and I

annotation.surface: A match report: a defender turned back to cover, with his side 5-1 up.
annotation.walkthrough: The football surface makes 5-1 a scoreline; it is Roman numerals V and I, placed after A.
annotation.definitionFit: A saviour is one who rescues or defends others.

entries.clue: Achievement in martial arts something to build upon? Not ideally (9)

annotation.definition2: something to build upon? Not ideally

blocks.note: a coloured grade awarded in judo or karate

blocks.clueFragment: something to build upon? Not ideally
blocks.note: the protected countryside round a town, where building is discouraged

annotation.surface: A martial arts grade is treated as a foundation to build on, with doubts.
annotation.walkthrough: In Britain the green belt is land ringing a town where development is restricted, hence 'not ideally' something to build on.
annotation.definitionFit: A green belt is both a coloured belt rank and a zone of protected open land.

entries.clue: Go off to collect a small piece of meat (5)

indicatorNotes.to collect: ROT gathers A and S inside it

blocks.note: S = small, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: Someone sets off to pick up a bit of meat from the butcher.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Go off' reads as setting out; it means to spoil.
annotation.definitionFit: A roast is a joint of meat cooked in the oven.

entries.clue: I’m surprised — small figure’s brought in by top earner (5-7)

indicatorNotes.brought in: to bring someone in is to admit them, so MY lets ONE inside

blocks.note: a spinning top is a spinner

annotation.surface: Someone is amazed to see a small figure being brought in by the company's highest earner.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Top earner' looks like one phrase; split it, since 'top' is the toy, SPINNER, and 'earner' alone is the definition. The 's is 'is': the small figure is brought in.
annotation.definitionFit: A money-spinner is something that earns a lot, a nice little earner.

entries.clue: Under pressure, worked shifts say, in potentially dangerous situation (6,3)

indicatorNotes.Under: in a down clue the rest sits under P

annotation.surface: Workers under strain put in long shifts in a volatile setting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Worked shifts' reads as factory rotas; 'shifts' is the verb that rearranges WORKED.
annotation.definitionFit: A powder keg is a barrel of gunpowder, and figuratively a situation ready to explode.

entries.clue: Fighter with precipitate manoeuvre, ultimately leading to painful episode (8)

blocks.note: the MiG, a Russian fighter jet
to precipitate is to fall as rain

annotation.surface: A fighter pilot's reckless move ends in a painful incident.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Precipitate manoeuvre' reads as a rash move; 'precipitate' is the weather verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A migraine is an attack of severe headache.

entries.clue: A hair product I’m regularly into — you’re never too old, unless it’s applied (3,5)

annotation.definition: you’re never too old, unless it’s applied
annotation.surface: An older person boasts about a hair product they are into, since no one is too old.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a playful description: without an age limit, no one is too old; one applied can make you so.
annotation.definitionFit: An age limit is the age beyond which you are excluded, the only thing that makes you 'too old'.

entries.clue: Grunting, chew nuts — awful! (3-9)

indicatorNotes.nuts: crazy, so the letters go wild

annotation.surface: Someone grunts while chewing nuts, and it is horrible to listen to.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chew nuts' paints a snack; 'nuts' is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Gut-wrenching means deeply distressing, awful.

entries.clue: Caught traffic light about to change, arriving at curve in road (6)

blocks.note: the amber light shows just before red

annotation.surface: A driver is caught by a changing light just as they reach a bend.
annotation.walkthrough: The driving surface runs straight through to the road-building definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A camber is the slight curve across a road's surface that lets water drain off.

entries.clue: Hunter erected a place to sleep in (6)

indicatorNotes.erected: set upright, so in a down clue it reads bottom to top

annotation.surface: A hunter puts up a shelter to sleep in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Erected a place to sleep' pictures pitching a tent; 'erected' just stands DORM IN on its head.
annotation.definitionFit: Nimrod is the mighty hunter of Genesis, and his name stands for any hunter.

entries.clue: “Excuse me from meal”, I repeated, interjecting “Bravo!” (5)

indicatorNotes.from: ME is taken away from MEAL
indicatorNotes.interjecting: B is thrown in between the two Is

blocks.note: Bravo is B in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: Someone keeps asking to leave the dinner table while another guest shouts applause.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Excuse me' reads as a polite phrase; 'Excuse' alone is the definition and 'me from meal' is an instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: An alibi is an excuse, strictly a claim to have been elsewhere.

entries.clue: Fugitive’s fantastic leap across border — Steve, actor featuring at the end (9)

indicatorNotes.fantastic: wildly altered, so LEAP and ER are rearranged
indicatorNotes.across: the rearranged letters stretch across HEM
indicatorNotes.at the end: take the final letters of 'Steve' and 'actor'
indicatorNotes.featuring: to feature is to be included, so those end letters join the fodder

blocks.note: last letters of stevE and actoR, joining the fodder
a hem is the border of a garment

annotation.surface: A runaway makes a wild leap over a frontier, like Steve McQueen in the film's final scene.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Steve McQueen's motorbike leap at the border in The Great Escape. 'Fugitive' is the adjective, fleeting, not the runaway.
annotation.definitionFit: Fugitive can mean fleeting or short-lived, which is what ephemeral means.

entries.clue: Maybe old farm worker’s beginning to regret cutting into pipe (5)

indicatorNotes.cutting into: a cut goes into the thing it slices, so R lands inside HOSE

blocks.note: a hose is a flexible pipe

annotation.surface: An old farmhand starts to regret slicing through a pipe.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old farm worker' suggests a labourer; it is the animal, once the farm's main source of pulling power. 'Maybe' flags it as an example.
annotation.definitionFit: Before tractors, horses did much of the heavy work on farms.

entries.clue: Crazy fool keeps on grabbing son (7)

indicatorNotes.keeps: to keep something is to hold on to it, so BERK holds the rest inside
indicatorNotes.grabbing: what is grabbed ends up in the grabber's grip, so RE closes round S

blocks.note: berk is British slang for a fool

annotation.surface: A mad fool keeps snatching at a boy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Keeps on' reads as 'continues'; split it, since 'keeps' is the container signal and 'on' gives RE.
annotation.definitionFit: Berserk means wildly out of control, crazy.

entries.clue: Accuracy is maintained by compass (7)

indicatorNotes.is maintained by: to maintain is to keep and hold, so REALM keeps IS within it

blocks.note: compass = scope or range, a realm

annotation.surface: A compass keeps a traveller on course.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Compass' suggests the navigator's tool; here it means range or domain.
annotation.definitionFit: Realism in art or writing is faithful accuracy to life.

entries.clue: Journalist, left outside, changed plans (10)

indicatorNotes.outside: the word for left stands on the outside, wrapping round the journalist

blocks.note: to leave a job is to resign

annotation.surface: A journalist who left the paper altered their plans.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like the political side or L; it is the verb, resigned.
annotation.definitionFit: To redesign is to change the plans for something.

entries.clue: Hide pepper (4)

blocks.note: an animal's skin with the fur
to pepper someone is to bombard them with missiles

annotation.walkthrough: Both words look like other parts of speech: 'Hide' is the noun, skin, and 'pepper' the verb, bombard.
annotation.definitionFit: A pelt is a hide, and to pelt someone is to pepper them with blows or objects.
